Wherever possible, URL based codes should be sent as "fragment" parameters (after the #) as these are not sent to the server but are still accessible via local JavaScript so that they can be processed. Maybe we just need to clarify this:


> Verify that sensitive data is only sent to the server in the HTTP message body or headers and that the URL and query string do not contain sensitive information, such as an API key or session token. **Where sensitive data needs to be contained in a link such as a password reset token, this should be included as a "fragment" parameter after the # symbol so that it is not directly transmitted to the server.**
